detail.title: gown; cloth

The cloth has been folded in halves and the stitching removed along the centre to create a hole for the head, in order to form a crude sleeveless tunic by sewing the sides together while leaving holes for the arms. A second pair of heddles has been used to create solid bands of weft decoration which have been woven in at irregular intervals along each strip; these are composed of lines of red, blue, yellow and white cotton. detail.title: garment; cloth
detail.description:
Wrapper; hand-woven plain weave cotton cloth with supplementary weft in rayon thread. Composed of 21 narrow warp-faced strips machine-sewn together at the selvedges. Two alternating strips: blue and white cotton warp with black cotton and gold rayon weft; banded border at each end with continuous supplementary weft patterns in blue and gold rayon. Red cotton warp and weft; banded border at each end with supplementary weft in gold rayon. Unworked warp fringe on all strips.

Main design elements worked in discontinuous supplementary weft in multi-coloured rayon thread. Designs include: diamond, chameleon, bird, sword, key, quadruped, butterfly. These mainly representational motifs are set within a larger diamond formed from 24 rectangles arranged in stepped pattern across the strips. Rectangles are worked in discontinuous supplementary weft: blue and gold rayon on the red strips; burgundy and gold rayon on the blue and white strips.

detail.title: hammock

detail.title: hammock
detail.description: Hammock; made of cotton, hand-woven in four narrow strips which have been sewn together along the selvedges. The cotton is mostly hand-spun and locally dyed, though the red and black appears to be European imported thread. The warp is of white cotton, and the weft uses a mixture of white, green, red and black cotton to form bands of decoration across the cloth. The two inner strips have a long area of white tufts of cotton along the centre; in the two outer strips these are replaced either by bands of decoration of the same kind as is seen at the ends of the cloth, or by designs in the shape of 'wine glasses' formed from discontinuous supplementary black thread. Along both sides a long fringe of white cotton openwork terminating in bobbles has been sewn on.
detail.production_ethnic_attribution: Made by: Mende (This hammock came from the Methodist Missionary Society together with many other items which appear to have been made by the Mende.)

1907.02.0034 Redjof, Övre Kongo Birma, Övre Kongo. [[Haga]] skiss Mangbetu? Horisonter - Musik Mangbetu Cittra.
Köpt Sjökapten I. Kjellman Birma, övre Kongo, Afrika Vit beläggning/smuts på halsen. Strängarna är lösa och sköra. Stämskruvarna, 5 st, är lösa. Annars god kondition. [[från utställning]] Northern Belg. Congo (perhaps Mangbetu). W.B.Fagg. 30.9.57 [[från utställning]] Northern Belg. Congo (perhaps Mangbetu). W.B.Fagg. 30.9.57

De nycklar ( 5 till antalet) som använts för att spänna strängarna är lösa från objektet. Cittra. Köpt
Längd: 52,5 cm, Bredd: 25,5 cm, Höjd: 27 cm 
Ursprung: Bi

Esa característica causó la sorpresa de los primeros exploradores europeos, costumbre  que, tradicionalmente, se practicaba en los bebés a los que se presionaba las cabezas con fuertes paños, para provocar la deformación craneal que les daría ese aspecto de adultos. Esa práctica desaparecería a partir de la década de 1950 con el proceso de occidentalización.

detail.title: print; satirical print; book-illustration
detail.description:
Plate from the 'Scourge', ii. 263 (second state). Members of the Court of Examiners of the Royal College of Surgeons sit on the outer side of a horse-shoe table, four on each side of the Master, who sits in a raised chair, wearing a gown, bands, and hat. On the table before him are a skull and bone. The examinee, trembling and insignificant, stands on the extreme left, facing a man who has risen from his chair to say angrily, "Describe, the Organs of Hearing"; the latter's neighbour listens intently through an ear-trumpet. The next Examiner sleeps with folded arms; next, and on the Master's right, is a man turning his back on the Master and holding his nose while he studies a book: 'Question upon Wind I Suppose a man was to . . . What w . . . you . . .' The aged and toothless Master (Sir Charles Blicke, 1745-1815) listens with senile intensity through an ear-trumpet. On his left two Scots, ungainly fellows wearing tartan, are absorbed in conversation; one says: "you paid too dear for it brother Sergeant," the other takes snuff from a mull. Next is a fat man with swathed gouty legs; crutches lie on the ground beside him; he has a paper 'THH [sic] COW POX CRONICLE', suggesting that he is Jenner (not a surgeon). He has a pen in his mouth, spectacles on forehead, and looks sideways at his neighbour, a lean old man who is intently counting piles of coin. In the foreground is a trough containing books; a man stands near it holding a large volume and looking towards examiner and examinee. A man leaves the room (right) looking over his shoulder with shocked distress, and exclaiming "Oh!" In his pocket is a paper: 'A Peter on the Gravel'.
The Master's chair is decorated with skulls; from its back projects a striped pole supporting a skull which serves as a wig-block, emblem of the old connexion between surgeons and barbers, see No. 9092, &c. Under the chair are money-bags, one inscribed '£50', the other 'For Shirt'. Behind the chair are two niches or alcoves in each of which a skeleton is suspended by the neck from a rope; one (left) is 'Govenor [sic] Wall' [see No. 9845], the other 'Lady Brownrigg'. These are symmetrically flanked by four pictures: [1] a prizefight between a black pugilist and a skeleton at which the Master of the College presides, standing before his chair. [2] Saartjie Baartman, 'the Hottentot Venus', see No. 11577, &c., stands in profile to the right while 'Nobody', a man whose legs are jointed to his shoulders as in No. 12438, &c., points with amusement at her huge posterior. [3] A young woman without arms or legs, placed on a bergere, is inspected by an ugly man, who points at her. [4] A brazen cow (or golden calf) is supported on a garlanded pillar on whose base is a crown; round this men, apparently surgeons, dance gleefully, holding hands in a ring. On the extreme left of the wall is an ornate clock, showing that the time is eleven. It is topped by a grinning figure of Time holding an hourglass. On the ground is a paper: 'At the sign of the Cow's Head Lincolns Inn Feilds'.
1 October 1811
Hand-coloured etching

He wears a loose fur-collared coat or gown over breeches and waistcoat. He leans back reflectively, an open book, Diversions of Purley [by Home Tooke, cf. BM Satires 9020], in his right hand. Phases of his past life are illustrated in a series of W.L. portraits on the wall behind him. [1] As a handsome young man he stands holding a long-bow, as if at an archery contest. [2] He stands, slightly obese, in his Light Horse uniform, see BM Satires 8800 (1796). [3] He stands in back view as in BM Satires 12803, facing a wall on which is a portrait of the Hottentot Venus [Saartjie Baartman], see BM Satires 11577, &c. [4] He stands in hussar uniform, with high curled wig and whiskers. [5] He stands directed to the right in Field Marshal's uniform (as 'especially in 1814). [6] He stands on the deck of a ship in yachting costume wearing loose jacket and trousers, his hands in his coat-pocket. The profile and paunch of Sir William Curtis are behind and on the extreme left. [7] The picture is partly concealed by a curtain, but the King sits near a chamber-pot. [8] He stands in coronation robes holding orb and sceptre (see BM Satires 14199). [9] He is in Highland costume (see BM Satires 14386). At the King's left hand is a small cheval-glass topped by a crown. His appearance has changed, he has no whiskers, and has a wig of lightly curled natural hair, parted in the middle, so that in place of the pear- or pineapple-shaped head resulting from a crest of curls and whiskers, as from c. 1811 [In caricature. An engraved H.L. portrait by Schiavonetti after T. Phillips, pub. Cadell & Davis, 11 Oct. 1809, has whiskers and crest of curls], his face seems rounder, and, in many prints, younger. His dress is less formal, and his appearance (confirmed by portraits from 1820) suggests a determination to depart completely from the appearance and costume of caricature.  March 15 1824
Hand-coloured etching

detail.title: print; satirical print
detail.description:
Frontispiece from 'Metropolitan Grievances; or, a serio-comic glance at minor mischiefs in London and its Vicinity', 1812 (in Print Room). A crowded street scene, with the corner of a tripe-butcher's on the right: 'Gilbert. Gall Tripem[an]', a lean-to shop, in which the butcher bargains over sheeps' trotters and offal with an elderly woman. Outside this is a pavement along which a little boy bowls a hoop between the legs of an elderly lady on the extreme right who totters on high-heeled shoes, having dropped a lap-dog from her muff. A little chimney-sweep is much amused. Above the butcher's a woman at a window empties a pan: the contents splash on to the pent-house roof and pour through a spout over the white stockings of a fashionably dressed passer-by who registers horror, holding up an eyeglass. The stream splashes the unconscious woman who chaffers with the tripe-man. A street-lamp projecting from the corner of the house is broken. Over the uneven cobbles an old woman pushes a barrow of cat's-meat, shrieking her wares; two dogs bark at the barrow, a cat miaows. Near her stands a ragged, bare-legged man, with grievously twisted and misshapen legs (showing the effects of rickets); he sells 'The Last Dying Sp[eech] . . .', with a print of bodies on a gibbet, shouting from a cavernous mouth in a subhuman face. Behind him a jovial crossing-sweeper plies his broom. On the left is a caricature shop, the window-panes filled with prints, among which one of 'the Hottentot Venus', Saartjie Baartman, see No. 11577, &c., is conspicuous. There are also large comic heads. A fashionably dressed woman leaves the shop, holding her nose (assailed by the cat's-meat). Four men gaze at the window; one is a countryman whose pocket is being picked. Heavy flower-pots are about to fall on their heads from a projecting ledge. A woman leans from a first-floor window trying vainly to stop the fall, and letting her watering-pot discharge its contents on the still unconscious window-gazers. On the wall is the disk of the 'Sun' Fire Office, with the date '1812'. The next house is a small gin-shop with a bunch of grapes for its sign and the inscription '. . Arsnic—Best Cordial Gin'. Three dram-drinkers stand at the door. The last house, a corner one, is dilapidated and shored up with a beam. The ground floor belongs to 'D. Dip Tallow Chandler'; against the window is a stall or bulk. The top floor is that of 'Ling—Dyer &c'; a pole projects from a window with dyed garments and a length of material hanging out to dry. On the corner of the house is the notice: 'F P 20 Ft'. In the background the dome of St. Paul's rises above the roofs of houses in the middle distance.
c. 1812.
Hand-coloured etching.

detail.title: print; book; book-illustration
detail.description:
A book of prints by Samuel Daniell, illustrative of southern African animals, peoples and scenery, titles and a production detail to each plate, a descriptive text prefacing every three images. The individual plates as follows:

1. The title-page to the first part, the text on a large rock with a lion skin draped over it, two native tribesmen on either side, one bearing a shield and spear and the other crouching with his bow, an aloe to the left
2. A view of a Khoikhoi (or Hottentot) village of the Korah tribe on the banks of the Orange River, tribesmen crossing the river with their sheep on submerged logs and another driving his flock to the water, cattle beyond, goats and a reclining figure before a wicker hut, trees lining the shore of the river
3. Three San (or Bushmen) hunters armed with bows and arrows and clothed only in loincloths, two standing with elaborate head-dresses and the other reclining with an ostrich feather plume in his hair, a dog and an ostrich egg at their feet, a woman beyond with her children, huts and other San to the right by their campfires, other people on the plains beyond at the foot of the mountains in the distance
4. A white-tailed gnu (Connochaetes gnou) standing on a rocky outcrop pawing at the ground, other wildebeest and hartebeest grazing to the left, ostriches beyond and a hunt in the distance, mountains beyond
5. A view of a native (possibly Zulu) village on the banks of a small lake, huts on the low hills and at the water's edge, cattle watering in the lake and walking down the slope beyond, tribesmen and women going about their business, mountains beyond
6. Native tribesmen (possibly Zulus) on a march, two warriors to the foregorund armed with spears and shields and with elaborate headresses, a woman mounted on an ox and another cow being tended by a tribesman, other natives beyond with their cattle in the wooded landscape
7. Three greater kudu (Tragelaphus strepsiceros), a male, female and a reclining juvenile, wooded cliffs behind and a hunt in the distance
8. A view of a Tswana hut  surrounded by a high wall, two women, a child and a man gathered round the cooking fire in the courtyard, the child playing with a dog and one of the women preparing food, other dwellings on the hill beyond with cattle under the shade of the trees
9. Tswana people, a woman with a child tied to her back and an adze over her shoulder, a warrior and another child seated on a leopard-skin to the right and a woman smoking from a horn pipe behind, other tribesmen tending their cattle or shading themselves with palm fronds beyond, a village in the distance
10. A male impala (Aepyceros melampus) and a reclining female and baby beyond, a stream to the right and spreading trees to the left, other impala in the shade beyond
11. A view of the new theatre and Hottentot Square (now Riebeeck Square) in Cape Town, a mounted settler accompanied by native guides riding after a cart pulled by a team of oxen, two natives in conversation to the foreground, people going about their business beyond, Table Mountain in the distance
12. Two mounted Boers and their party returning from the hunt, one dressed in a blue coat and wide hat with his rifle slung at his side and a gray rhebok over his saddle, a native servant walking behind carrying a rifle and a dead springhare by the feet, a dog at his side, two other natives and a waggon drawn by horses beyond, the house to the right with a Boer man and woman waiting on the veranda
13. A common hippopotamus (Hippopotamus amphibius), others in the water to the left and amongst the reeds, a hunting party in the distance
14. A view of the military station at Algoa Bay, the small European building to the left and flying an ensign, cattle at the water's edge of an inlet leading out to the sea beyond, a boat on the water
15. Four bust-length portraits of native people, two Khoikhoi and two described as 'kaffirs' (possibly Zulus)
16. A quagga (Equus quagga quagga), another quagga and a foal grazing behind, common eland on the hill beyond and a larger herd of quagga and ostriches to the right, a Boar attempting to capture a quagga beyond, mountains in the distance
17. The title-page to the second part, the text on a zebra skin being fought over by two flying vultures, other vultures circling in the sky beyond
18. A view of a Boer settler's house, a lake to the foreground with a waggon drawn up at the water's edge, herdsmen to the right driving a flock of sheep and goats with two cattle, sheep on the mountains beyond
19. A Boer camp with two men seated and smoking pipes under an awning rigged from their waggon and using a long whip and a rifle as struts, a woman and her child asleep on a bed roll, chickens, guinea fowl and a tame antelope about the family, a pet baboon in the covered waggon, cattle, native servants and another waggon beyond
20. A springbok (Antidorcas marsupialis) with a reclining baby at its feet, other springbok resting behind, a large herd of the antelope and some ostriches beyond and a Boer house in the distance
21. A view of a heavily forested lake in Tsitsikamma, a herd of (incorrect) Asian elephants wading and grazing in the water, flamingoes on the banks, the trees with creepers winding up the trunks, gourds hanging from the branches
22. A family of Khoikhoi of the Korah tribe packing their belongings and striking their hut, a man taking down the struts of the tent and another folding the matting walls, a woman holding an ox by a rope with baggage tied onto the back of the animal, a dog running to the left, a lake and woods beyond
23. A giant forest hog (Hylochoerus meinertzhageni), another lying in the reeds by the water's edge, fallen trees and a forested bank behind, a hunter with dogs attacking a hog in the jungle beyond
24. A view of the Tswana town of Leetakoo, native huts surrounded by high walls on a cliff and others below with kraals on either side of the wide river, cattle by the water's edge, mountains beyond
25. Tswana women engaged in making pottery, one woman shaping a new kiln with her child bringing more clay to her, another woman sitting beyond by a kiln making pots, a child climbing up the side of the high kiln, a cooking pot on the fire to the right, the area surrounded by a high rush wall, another hut beyond
26. A bluebuck (Hippotragus leucophaeus), another drinking at the lake beyond, giraffes and more of the antelope grazing in the distance
27. A view of a large waterfall on the Sneeuberge cascading from the high cliffs, trees on the banks of the river and the rocks beyond, a lion and lioness on the small beach and storks feeding in the shallows, antelope running along the shore
28. A San man and woman frying locusts in an earth pit, the man with porcupine quills stuck into his hair and stirring the insects, the woman looking on, a small matting shelter beyond and a child asleep on a rug to the left, other San with their shelters to the right and herds of quagga and antelope beyond, mountains in the distance
29. A klipspringer (Oreotragus oreotragus) standing on a high cliff-top, vultures on the slopes below and circling in the air, another klipspringer on the summit in the distance
30. A view of the Lion's Head Mountain, near Cape Town, a European house to the left with steps leading up to the door and a baboon chained on a long pole, an aloe plant and other trees to the right, trees and rocks on the mountain beyond
31. Four bust-length portraits of native people, two San and two Bechuanas
32. A black rhinoceros (Diceros bicornis), a small pond to the right with two huntsmen and their dogs attacking two other rhinoceroses in the reeds, mountains beyond

detail.title: marriage equipment
detail.description:
Marriage bed-screen,  Hand-woven tapestry type piece. The piece is rectangular and composed of seven narrow strips hand-sewn together selvedge to selvedge. Warp and weft are made of industrial white and coloured cotton threads. 

The piece is executed in plain-weaving with the motifs made in supplementary weft work.  The threads at the ends of the strips are twisted and knotted to form tassels.

The decoration is organised in white and coloured bands with transverse continued weft-faced arrangement. Three bands have lozenge-shaped motifs. In the centre of the piece is a saffron-yellow background band with a motif in the form of a lozenge made of a series of red, black and white oval figures. On both borders of the saffron-yellow band is a multicoloured band with black and white lozenges and saffron-yellow and red half-lozenges made in supplementary weft work. 

On both sides between the central band and the end of the piece is a red band with a motif in the form of a lozenge prolonged by two bars. On both borders of the red bands is a multicoloured band made of saffron-yellow, light-green, black, red and white lozenges made in supplementary weft work. 

Between the bands with the lozenge-shaped motifs and between them and the ends of the piece are alternating black, white, saffron-yellow, red and light-green bands, and a blue bands, some of which are decorated with black, saffron-yellow, red and light-green oval figures.

detail.title: marriage equipment; wall-hanging
detail.description:
Marriage wall-hanging, hand-woven tapestry type piece. The piece is rectangular and composed of eleven narrow strips hand-sewn together selvedge to selvedge. Warp is made of white cotton threads. Weft is made of industrial white cotton threads and black, yellow, red and green synthetic wool threads. Supplementary weft work is made of black, yellow, and red synthetic wool threads.

The piece is executed in plain-weaving with the motifs made in supplementary weft work.  The strips end in loose warp threads. The background of the piece is white. The decoration is organised in black and coloured bands with transverse continued weft-faced arrangement, symmetrically displayed. 

In the centre of the piece is a composition organised on both sides of a narrow band with a black background made in supplementary weft-work using synthetic wool, with a border of black and white squares and bars, and a central design in the form of a lozenge formed by a series of white, yellow and red ovals. Symmetrically displayed on both sides from the central black band is a succession of narrow plain-weave yellow, green and red bands (the latter decorated with un-worked yellow, black and red wool threads), and a white band decorated with black lozenge and bars made in supplementary weft-work, followed by plain weave black, white, green, red and black bands. 

Symmetrically displayed from the central composition is a succession of a white background band decorated with black lozenges followed by a black-background band with a chess-board decoration and green, yellow, red and black borders. The chess-board band is followed by a succession of white background bands decorated with lozenges and triangles, and of plain-weave white, red and black bands.

Towards both ends of the piece is a composition repeating the central composition, less a plain-weave green band. Between those compositions and the end of the piece are two black parallel bars.  

The two strips have more simplified decoration of mostly plain-weave coloured bands and bars. A black band close to the centre is decorated with a chess-board style lozenge made of white, red and black squares.

detail.title: textile
detail.description:
Textile consisting of six narrow strip woven cotton lengths, hand sewn together selvedge to selvedge. Ground weave: plain weave: dyed blue cotton warps and dyed blue and white cotton wefts. There are also a number of silver tinsel wefts thorughout the cloth.  This creates a cloth with a dark blue background with bands of weft stripes at either end in white with a silver 'sparkle.' The cloth is then decorated using supplementary weft and supplementary weft floats in white. There is a band of white check at each end of the cloth flanked by the white stripes mentioned earlier. The central panel consists of six warp stripes which are decorated with chains of diamonds consisting of warp lines. These diamonds are backed by black and white check bordered by white warp stripes. There is, throughout the whole cloth, a sprinkling of sparkle created by the small amounts of tinsel woven into the cloth.

The textile is finished in unworked warps.

At the front is sewn an irregularly shaped pocket of the same material. Both the front and the back are extensively embroidered with hand-sewn decoration in white, green, peach, red, light blue, dark blue and yellow European cotton thread, in patterns that include knives, stars and spirals. The decoration on the front is asymmetrical; that on the back is symmetrical. The sleeves and base are hemmed by machine.

detail.description: Cloth composed of 29 very narrow strips of two different widths, hand-woven from imported European thread, and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The warp ends have been left loose and twisted and knotted to form a fringe.

1983.23.0009 statussymbol Helena Valley, Montana,USA Helena Valley, Montana skiss Ojibwa Amerika United States Ojibwe Halsprydnad, s.k. choka, i pärlstickning i röda och vita fält åtskilda av läderbitar. I centrum har en konkav, run rosa platta (knapp) fästs på vilken sitter två kulor av gulmetall och från vars baksida det hänger två korta snören med på vilken det trätts en cylindrisk pärla och i ytterkant 
knutits en snäcka. 
L: ca 32,5cm, B: 3,5 cm. 
Används enligt insamlaren som statussymbol för bl.a. Ojibwa. Köp av Josef Lagergren

detail.title: Quechquémitl met geometrische motieven
detail.description:
Deze quechquémitl is waarschijnlijk in een heupweefgetouw geweven met katoen. Er zijn versieringen aangebracht in de vorm van borduursels, door gebruik te maken van de kruissteek. Een borduursel is een decoratieve techniek waarbij extra draden aan het weefsel worden toegevoegd. 

De achtergrondskleur is wit. De quechquémitl is in het geheel versierd met geometrische motieven in verschillende kleuren.

Huipiles en quechquémitl (voor beide kledingstukken zijn geen goede equivalenten in de Nederlandse taal te vinden) zijn de traditionele kledingstukken bij uitstek van de Indiaanse vrouw in Mexico

Canada 1904.19.0138 America Anna och Gustaf Retzius resa till Nordamerika (1893) Detta är en läpp-prydnad i trä, inlagd med haliotiskal. Proveniensen är angiven som British Columbia.

detail.title: saddle-bag
detail.description: A double saddle-bag made of leather, each capacious bag fastened with leather drawstring.  Each bag flap and narrow 'neck' between decorated with applied blue and thinner red tabby cotton cloth.  Red cloth narrows to piping between two bags.  Identical beadwork on each flap: cross (+) in the centre, with six stylized human (?) figures beside cloth border.  Worked in red, green and black glass beads, with transparent and light blue beads used near the 'neck'.  Two round metal discs on each motif.  Small diamond motifs between arms of cross and on two sides.  Red and blue glass beads suspended on leather strips from shaped bag edge.
